info.title: Universal file converter
info.summary: Converts documents, spreadsheets, presentations and images using LibreOffice headless.
info.description:
Uploads a file and receives it converted to another format.

## The contract

This API is consumed by a **shipped Android client**, so the following
properties are part of the contract and are not free to change.

> **Breaking change: `POST /convert` without a target no longer exists.**
> Clients must post to `/convert/pdf`. A client still using the bare path
> gets the catch-all `404`, whose message tells the user to update the app.

- **Success is `200` with the target's own media type.** For `pdf` that is
  exactly `application/pdf`, with no charset suffix: the client compares the
  header and refuses anything else, so a stray `text/html` on a `200` is a
  client-visible failure.
- **Failure is a non-2xx with the JSON error envelope.** The client reads
  `error.message` and shows it verbatim in a dialog, falling back to
  `"HTTP <status>"` when the body is missing or is not JSON.
- **A failure is never a `200`.** The client checks the status before it
  reads anything, so a `200` is treated as the converted file and fails
  downstream.
- **`error.message` is user-facing prose.** It is a complete sentence with
  no stack traces, no paths and no codes, because a person reads it.
  `error.code` is for logs and metrics only; the client never displays it.

## Choosing the output format

The target is part of the path and is REQUIRED: `/convert/pdf`,
`/convert/xlsx`, `/convert/png`. There is deliberately no bare `/convert`
that assumes a format - one address that means one thing is easier to
document and to test than two that mean the same thing.

**Not every source can become every target.** The matrix is finite and
deliberate - `GET /formats` returns it in full, machine-readably. Asking for
a target that exists but is not reachable from your file is a `415`; asking
for a target that does not exist at all is a `404`. Both messages list the
alternatives, so a client never has to hard-code the table to give a useful
error.

## Filenames

The response offers the uploaded file's name with the new extension:
`Quarterly report.docx` converted to `pdf` downloads as
`Quarterly report.pdf`. The name is sanitised before it is echoed - path
segments and control characters are removed - and a name with nothing usable
in it becomes `converted.<ext>`.

## Image targets are archives

`png` and `jpg` produce **one image per page**, so they answer with
`application/zip` holding `slide-1.png`, `slide-2.png`, ... This is true even
for a one-page document: the content type must not depend on how many pages
the upload happened to have, or every client has to sniff what it received.

## Timing

The client aborts the whole request after **120 seconds**. The server's own
deadline is **90 seconds** and covers the entire pipeline - including the
render-then-rasterise second step an image target needs - so that it can
still answer with a proper `504` instead of being killed mid-conversion.

## Uploads

Requests are `multipart/form-data` with exactly one file part. The import
filter is chosen from the **filename extension**, never from the declared
MIME type: the client deliberately sends `application/octet-stream`, and a
hostile client could declare anything at all.

post.summary: Convert a file to a named format
post.description:
Converts the upload to `target`, which must be an id from
`GET /formats` (`pdf`, `odt`, `docx`, `txt`, `html`, `rtf`, `epub`,
`ods`, `xlsx`, `csv`, `odp`, `pptx`, `png`, `jpg`).

The document is parsed by LibreOffice, which is a large C++ codebase
handling untrusted input. **Treat a conversion failure as an expected,
normal event**, not as an incident.

The endpoint is unauthenticated and cannot be otherwise: the client is
an APK, so any secret shipped inside it is public. Requests are
rate-limited per IP and conversions run under a bounded concurrency
limit; both are sources of `429` and `503` that a well-formed request
can hit.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The format to produce. Case-sensitive, without a leading dot.

get.description:
Every source extension this service accepts, and every target each one
can become.

Exists so a client does not have to hard-code the table: the shipped
client is an APK, and without this, teaching it a new output format
would mean shipping a new APK. A client that hard-codes the matrix will
silently disagree with the server the first time the server grows.

sources.description: Accepted upload types, keyed by extension.

family.description:
The LibreOffice document family that handles it.
Sources in the same family convert the same way.

targets.description: Every format this service can produce.

label.description: Short name, as used in error messages.

multiple.description:
When true the response is a ZIP of one file per page
rather than a single file. Always an archive for
these, even for a one-page source.

get.description:
Returns `ok` once the service is ready to convert.

The service only begins listening after LibreOffice has been confirmed
on `PATH`, the rasteriser has been confirmed, the metric-compatible
fonts have been verified, and a warm-up conversion has succeeded **for
every document family** - so reaching this endpoint at all means the
whole matrix is ready, not merely that the process is up.

It does not exercise a conversion of its own.

Upload.description:
Exactly one file part named `file`. Additional parts, or a part under
a different name, are rejected with `400`.

The overall body limit is **26214400 bytes (25 MB)**, matching the
client's own `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` and the reverse proxy's body limit.
Exceeding it at any layer produces `413`.

file.description:
The file to convert. Its **filename extension** selects the
import filter and must be one of the extensions listed by
`GET /formats` (case-insensitive). The declared `Content-Type`
of this part is ignored.

The filename is never used as a path on disk: the upload is
written to a server-generated name inside a per-request
temporary directory, so a name like `../../etc/passwd.docx`
is harmless.

TargetId.description:
Identifier of an output format, as used in the `/convert/{target}` path
and returned by `GET /formats`.

ErrorCode.description:
Stable machine-readable identifier for the failure. For logs, metrics
and support only - the client never shows this to the user.

ErrorEnvelope.description:
The body of every non-2xx response. There are no exceptions: error
paths that Express or multer would normally render as an HTML page are
overridden to produce this shape.

message.description:
A complete sentence shown verbatim in a dialog on the phone.
Never a stack trace, a file path or a bare code.

X-Request-Id.description:
Identifier for this request, also present in the server log line.
Quote it when reporting a problem.

ConvertedToTarget.description:
The converted file.

The media type is the target's own - `application/pdf` for `pdf`,
`text/csv` for `csv`, and so on. **The image targets are the exception**:
`png` and `jpg` always answer with `application/zip`, because there is
one image per page and a ZIP is the only way to put several files in one
response.

Content-Disposition.description:
The uploaded file's name with the target's extension. Sanitised:
path segments and control characters are stripped, and a name with
nothing usable in it becomes `converted.<ext>`.

Sent in both RFC 6266 forms - a quoted ASCII `filename` for older
clients and a percent-encoded UTF-8 `filename*` for current ones -
so a non-ASCII name survives.

BadRequest.description:
The request was not a usable upload: no file part named `file`, several
files, or a part under a different name.

error.message: The document could not be received. Please try again.

NotFound.description:
No such endpoint. In practice this means the client is older than the
server, which is why the message tells the user to update the app.

error.message: The converter is not available at this address. Please update the app and try again.

UnknownTarget.description:
The target in the path is not a format this service can produce at all -
`/convert/banana`. Distinct from a real target the source cannot become,
which is a `415`: this one is a `404` because the address does not exist.

error.message: That is not a format this converter can produce. Available: PDF, ODT, DOCX, TXT, HTML, RTF, EPUB, ODS, XLSX, CSV, ODP, PPTX, PNG, JPG.

TooLarge.description:
The upload exceeds 26214400 bytes (25 MB). Applied by the reverse proxy,
by the multipart parser and by the client, all using the same limit.

Also returned when an image target would produce more pages than the
server will hold in memory at once, which is a bound on the archive
rather than on the upload.

error.message: This document is too large to convert.

Unsupported.description:
The filename extension is not one this service accepts. The extension -
not the declared MIME type - selects the import filter.

The message lists the accepted extensions, because the person holding
the phone has a file they believe is a document, and "unsupported"
alone tells them nothing about what would work.

error.message: This file type cannot be converted. Supported types: .docx, .docm, .doc, .odt, .ods, .odp, .xlsx, .pptx, .csv, .txt, .html, .htm, .rtf, .png, .jpg, .jpeg.

UnsupportedTarget.description:
A real target, but not one this source can become - asking for `png`
from a `.docx`, say. This is a `415` and not a `404`, because the
address exists; it is the combination that does not.

The message names what the document CAN become instead, because the
useful answer to "can I have this as X" is "no, but here is what you can
have". The list varies by source, so the example below is the one for a
Word document; see `GET /formats` for the rest.

error.message: A .docx file can be converted to: PDF, ODT, TXT, HTML, RTF, EPUB.

Encrypted.description:
The document is password protected. Detected before LibreOffice runs,
because LibreOffice reports an encrypted document the same way it
reports a corrupt one, and telling a user their file is damaged when it
merely needs a password is both wrong and unhelpful.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests from this address in the current window.

error.message: Too many requests. Try again in a moment.

ConvertFailed.description:
The conversion produced nothing. Covers a damaged document, a document
whose content does not match its extension, and a zero-byte upload.

Note that LibreOffice's exit code is **not** used to decide this:
`--convert-to` exits `0` even when it converts nothing, so the only
trustworthy signal is whether a non-empty file of the expected type
appeared on disk.

error.message: This document could not be converted. It may be damaged or in a format the converter does not support.
Something went wrong on the server.

Busy.description:
Every conversion slot is taken and the waiting queue is full. Returned
immediately rather than queueing without bound, so the client gets a
fast, honest answer instead of a request that hangs until it times out.

error.message: The converter is busy. Try again in a moment.

Timeout.description:
The conversion exceeded the server's 90 second deadline. The running
LibreOffice process is sent `SIGTERM` and then `SIGKILL`.

This is deliberately shorter than the client's own 120 second abort, so
that the server answers with this response rather than being killed
mid-conversion and leaving the phone to report a network failure.

error.message: This document took too long to convert.
